title: How I Learned to Really Greet People
script: Narrator: [honestly] For years, my greetings were quick and empty. I said hello while looking at my phone, not at the person in front of me.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I did not think this was rude. I thought it was just normal, busy, modern life.
Narrator: [reflective] Then one day, an older neighbor greeted me properly. She stopped walking, looked at my eyes, and asked how my whole family was doing.
Narrator: [warmly] I was surprised. Nobody had greeted me like that in a long time. It only took thirty seconds, but I felt truly seen.
Narrator: [gently] That small moment stayed with me for days. I started noticing how careless my own greetings had become.
Narrator: [determined] So I decided to change something small. Whenever I greet someone now, I put my phone away first.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I try to say salaam clearly, look at the person, and actually listen to their answer, instead of already thinking about my reply.
Narrator: [honestly] At first, it felt strange and slow. I was used to rushing past people with a quick word.
Narrator: [gently] But slowly, something changed. People began smiling more when they saw me, and conversations felt warmer.
Narrator: [warmly] My grandmother always said a good greeting opens the door to a good relationship. I understand her now.
Narrator: [reflective] I also learned to greet elders first, and to use both hands when shaking hands with someone respected.
Narrator: [peacefully] These are small things, almost invisible, but they carry real meaning between people.
Narrator: [with a small smile] Now, when I meet someone, even a stranger, I try to greet them like they matter. Because they do.
Narrator: [gently] It costs nothing, this small kindness, yet it changes how a whole conversation begins.

quiz.question: How did the narrator usually greet people before this change?
options: Quickly and while looking at her phone
quiz.explanation: She says her greetings were quick and empty, said while looking at her phone.

quiz.question: What did the older neighbor do differently?
options: She stopped, looked at her eyes, and asked about her family
quiz.explanation: The neighbor stopped walking, made eye contact, and asked how the family was doing.

quiz.question: What did the narrator start doing before greeting people?
quiz.explanation: She decided to put her phone away first whenever greeting someone now.

quiz.question: What did people do more after her greetings changed?
options: Smiled more, and conversations felt warmer
quiz.explanation: She noticed people smiling more and conversations feeling warmer.

quiz.question: What does the narrator believe a good greeting does?
options: Opens the door to a good relationship
quiz.explanation: She recalls her grandmother's words that a good greeting opens the door to a good relationship.
